user.title: Connection Test
user.description: Adds the test endpoints, the dashboard card and the result sensors. There is nothing to configure here — payload sizes and how a device names itself are options on the card, because they describe the client being measured rather than the server.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Connection Test is already set up.

report.name: Report result
report.description: Records the result of a connection test run by a client. The card calls this automatically when a run finishes.

client_id.name: Client ID
client_id.description: Stable identifier for the device that ran the test. Results are keyed on this, so renaming a device updates its row instead of creating a second one.

client_name.name: Client name
client_name.description: Friendly name for the device, shown on the dashboard.

platform.name: Platform
platform.description: Which kind of client ran the test.

origin.name: Origin
origin.description: The URL the run measured. Which one was used changes what the result means.

page_origin.name: Page origin
page_origin.description: The URL the dashboard itself was loaded from, when the run measured a different one.

path.name: Path
path.description: Whether the client reached Home Assistant over the local network or from outside it.

user.name: User
user.description: The Home Assistant user logged in on that client.

user_agent.name: User agent
user_agent.description: The client's browser user agent string.

latency_samples_ms.name: Latency samples
latency_samples_ms.description: Raw round-trip times in milliseconds. The minimum, average, 95th percentile and jitter are derived from these.

http_latency_ms.name: HTTP latency
http_latency_ms.description: Round-trip time over plain HTTP, for comparison with the websocket figure.

download_seconds.name: Download duration
download_seconds.description: How long the download took, measured by the client.

download_streams.name: Download streams
download_streams.description: How many parallel connections the download used.

upload_seconds.name: Upload duration
upload_seconds.description: How long the upload took, measured by the client.
